items.title: Buster Williams interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 6, 2002
items.q: Kenny Andrews would come over and he and my father would practice and I’d sit there and I’d listen to them

ctx.x: Do you have an early — what’s your earliest recollection of your father playing gigs?

My earliest recollection of my father playing the bass is when I was a little boy. He used to sit on the sofa and put the bass between his legs and bow. One of his favorites was Slam Stewart. And my father — and Slam Stewart always had this, he developed this great bowing style, singing, the same phrases that he would play. And my father used to emulate that. And he was a great musician. He played piano and he also played drums. And so he was always playing music around the house. There was records, his musicians…
What kind of work was it? What kind of gigs was he playing, that he would take you out on? Were they club dates? Just dances? Things like that?
